subject: Clarify billing for long-context streaming and unit rounding
thread_summary: Customer asked how long context and streaming affect token billing, rounding, and minimums. Sales clarified billing quantum, caching behavior, and proposed a pilot concession and commit discount. External accepted and asked for procurement next steps.
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: billing units for streaming with long context

Hi Vanessa,

Quick one as we scope the integration: our product will stream incremental outputs to users while keeping a ~120k token conversation and document context (we've split into shards but still large). A few specific asks so procurement can model costs:

1) When we stream partial outputs (multiple chunks), do you charge the completion tokens as they generate, or is there any additional overhead for streaming?
2) For very long contexts (100k+ tokens) — are all input/context tokens billed per request? Any caching that would avoid recharging the same prefix across multiple requests?
3) What's Redwood's rounding/quantum and minimums per request? We need an example: if a single streaming response emits 620 tokens and we have a 50-token minimum or 10-token quantum — how would that be billed?

We'd also like to understand implications if we host in a dedicated capacity vs hosted.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Product
Acme Corp
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: billing units for streaming with long context

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear questions, happy to explain and give an example. TL;DR: streaming doesn't add a separate streaming-surcharge; tokens are metered the same way whether streamed or returned in a single chunk. I've attached a short spreadsheet with worked examples (billing-math.xlsx).

High level rules:
- Input/context tokens: billed when included in the request; if you send the same prefix verbatim in separate independent requests, each request is billed for those input tokens.
- KV/prefix caching: if you use our prefix caching (context buckets) and requests hit the same cached prefix, we bill the cached prefix once per active bucket refresh window rather than per request. This requires enabling context buckets (config on the project).
- Output tokens (completions): billed when generated. Streaming vs non-streaming is identical for metering — you pay for the same number of output tokens.
- Minimums & quantum: default minimum charge per inference call is 50 tokens. We round up output tokens to the nearest 10-token quantum for metering. Input tokens are billed at 1-token granularity. Example below.

Example (hosted API):
- Context included in request: 100,000 input tokens -> billed 100,000 tokens.
- Completion generated (streamed total): 620 tokens -> rounded to 630 (10-token quantum) and then compared to the 50-token minimum; charge = 630 output tokens.
- Total billed for that request = 100,000 + 630 = 100,630 tokens.

If you have multiple streaming chunks across the same session, we sum all generated tokens then apply the quantum rounding to the completion-side total once at the end-of-response accounting.

Dedicated capacity note: with Redwood Dedicated you can negotiate different quantums and minimums (commit-based tiers often have smaller quantum and lower/no minimums). Also, Dedicated supports local context bucket refreshes to reduce cross-request input charges.

If you want, I can propose two commercial options: (A) Hosted with standard metering above; (B) Enterprise committed plan with adjusted quantum/minimums and prefix-bucket pricing. I looped in Ben from Commercial to propose specific concessions.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: billing units for streaming with long context

Vanessa — thanks for the explanation. A couple commercial notes for the SOW:

- For an enterprise pilot at Acme with heavy long-context usage, recommend we:
  * Offer a 12% committed-use discount on token spend for a 6-month minimum spend (target: $250k/mo).
  * Temporarily waive the 50-token minimum for the pilot (first 3 months) so their engineering experiment doesn't get noisy billing.
  * Include a "context-bucket" add-on: for buckets > 50k tokens, apply a 10% reduction on input token bill for requests that hit the cached prefix. This encourages using our cache and reduces their unit cost.

- If procurement pushes on rounding quantum, we can reduce the output quantum from 10 -> 5 tokens for Dedicated customers at the commit level.

Laura — is the 6-month $250k/mo target workable for legal to scope in SOW? If not we can step down the discount or extend to 12 months.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: billing units for streaming with long context

Hi Liam — circling back with a proposed commercial packaging so your procurement team can review. Attached is a draft SOW (SOW_RBW-2247.pdf). Summary of the pricing points:

1) Metering baseline (hosted): input billed 1-token granularity; output rounded up to 10-token quantum; 50-token per-call minimum.
2) Pilot concession (applies to first 3 months): waive the 50-token minimum; apply a 12% committed-use discount on token spend (6-month minimum spend target $250k/mo).
3) Context-bucket add-on: if you enable context buckets and a request hits a cached prefix > 50k tokens, we apply a 10% discount on those input tokens. This is additive to the committed discount (multiplicative on cost).
4) Dedicated option: with a Dedicated capacity purchase we can reduce output quantum to 5 tokens and remove per-call minimums entirely for the contract term.

Next steps: if this is acceptable, can procurement confirm a PO window and whether they prefer Hosted+Pilot or a Dedicated trial? I can have legal update the SOW to reflect the selected option.

Thanks — attaching the worked examples we discussed.

Regards,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attached: SOW_RBW-2247.pdf, billing-math.xlsx)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: billing units for streaming with long context

Vanessa — this is great, thank you. Procurement prefers Hosted + Pilot to start (waive minimums for 3 months, 12% committed discount looks fine). We'll route the SOW through legal and aim to sign next week.

I'll loop in our SRE to kick off the context-bucket setup once SOW is live.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Product, Acme Corp
